summary: Tantalum nitride based thin films were deposited using thermal ALD with TaCp(=NtBu)(NEt2)2 and Ta(=NtBu)(NEt2)3 as precursors and ammonia as a reducing agent. The study focused on the influence of precursor structure on film stoichiometry, composition, and resistivity. The TaCp(=NtBu)(NEt2)2 precursor showed self-limiting growth in the 400–425 °C range with a growth rate of 0.51–0.91 Å cycle−1. The films were amorphous and exhibited lower resistivity due to the formation of tantalum carbide (TaC) from the Cp derivative.
evidence: TaNxCy self-limiting temperature dependent ALD growth was achieved for the TaCp(= N tBu)(NEt2)2/NH3 process with a growth rate of 0.51 –0.91 Å cycle −1 in the 400 –425 °C temperature range... The η5-cyclopentadienyl type compound allows lower nitrogen content in the precursor and thereafter in the deposited film... Since Ta –C bonds are present in the Cp derivative, the TaCp (= NtBu)(NEt2)2 tends more likely to form tantalum carbide compared to Ta(=NtBu)(NEt2)3, which leads to lower thin film resistivity.
